title: Over Characteristic Zero, Every Finite Etale Algebra of Rank at Least Three Is a Full Keller Fiber
summary: A quadratic-gauge proof and Lean formalization of prescribed full finite etale Keller fibres, with an explicit comparison to the earlier Ulam coefficient family.
verification: The characteristic-zero polynomial-presentation theorem and abstract finite-etale corollary have a Lean development; broader supplied-presentation scope has a separate assurance boundary.
next_steps: Obtain external review of the written proof and source/formal correspondence.
Complete specialist novelty review of the gauge and supplied-characteristic refinements; characteristic-zero existence is already a consequence of Ulam Theorem 5.2.
abstract:
A Keller map can only have finite \'etale fibers.  We ask the reverse
question: given a finite \'etale algebra, can it be made into the whole
fiber of such a map?  Over a field \(K\) of characteristic zero, the answer
is yes in every rank at least three.  More precisely, for every separable
polynomial \(P\in K[T]\) of degree \(N\geq3\), we construct a polynomial map
\(F_P:\A^3_K\to\A^3_K\) with \(\det DF_P=1\), geometric degree \(N\), and a
distinguished full fiber naturally isomorphic to \(\Spec K[T]/(P)\).

The characteristic-zero existence statement also follows by coefficient
specialization from the earlier all-degree family of Ulam. We give a
quadratic-gauge construction, a scheme-theoretic reconstruction and a
formalization of this consequence. The construction is read backwards.  A one-variable
inverse equation supplies a marked root; its derivative reconstructs the
source and, at the same time, is exactly the factor that cancels from the
Jacobian.  A translation inserts the prescribed polynomial into this
equation.  The characteristic-zero theorem---including the automatic
translation, function-field comparison, and abstract finite-\'etale
corollary---is formalized in Lean.  Over a field of characteristic different
from \(2\), the same formulas also give an explicit supplied-presentation
result whenever the first and third Hasse coefficients at the chosen
translation are nonzero.  That broader result commutes with scalar extension
and lies outside the end-to-end Lean formalization.  Choices made from an
abstract finite \'etale algebra are noncanonical.
